1.5.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation defines “Kekerasan” broadly (Pasal 1 angka 16) to include “penelantaran” (neglect) and “perlakuan buruk,” but it does not explicitly define or list “kekerasan ekonomi” (economic violence) against women as a violence type. The text does mention economic empowerment for women (Pasal 14) and “Anak yang Dieksploitasi secara Ekonomi” (Pasal 1 angka 21; Pasal 44 dst.), but that is child economic exploitation, not economic violence against women. Since the indicator is ‘Economic violence’ under scope_of_violence (typically about violence against women), the judge’s ‘No’ is reasonable given the available English and consistent with the Indonesian. Therefore the golden ‘Yes’ likely over-interprets economic empowerment/exploitation as ‘economic violence’.

1.6.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly includes prevention of child marriage, a harmful practice affecting girls.

CHAPTER I

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process that is systematically constructed to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access to and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy constructed to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget hereinafter abbreviated as ARG is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access to and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection of Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are disadvantaged, in frontier areas, and in outermost areas in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than other groups of Children. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and sexual abuse activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the human immune system until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Kidnapped Children are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state. 29. Child Victims of Sale are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons. 30.
